sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN lake.trips t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID AND t.payment_type = 2
GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The HASH_JOIN (node 8) performs a RIGHT join with filter pushdown on payment_type=2; DuckDB builds the hash table from the filtered trips (est. 99k rows) and probes the 265-row zones table, but the RIGHT join forces retention of all zone rows plus 99k matching trips, causing unnecessary row expansion before GROUP BY. The subsequent HASH_GROUP_BY then re-aggregates those 99k rows down to ~243 distinct PULocationIDs.

plan_nodes.note: Join Type: RIGHT | Conditions: CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID | Estimated Cardinality: 99167

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join lake.trips t on … and t.payment_type = 2)

Using a RIGHT hash join prevents filter pushdown into the build side and materializes 99k trip rows that immediately collapse to ~243 groups; switching to a LEFT join (zones LEFT JOIN filtered trips) or pre-aggregating trips by PULocationID before joining would eliminate the row expansion.

The SEQ_SCAN on trips reads all columns needed for the filter but projects only PULocationID; if payment_type is not in the same row group / segment, the scan still decodes full rows. A projection pushdown or columnar skip could reduce I/O.
